“Today a seedling – tomorrow a flower”
Meare Village Primary School aims to equip our pupils with the skills and mindset to thrive and take on the world.
By developing these skills and this mindset, we believe that our children will have success today and be prepared for tomorrow.
Our Classes

Headteacher’s Welcome Message
Welcome to Meare Village Primary School website!
“Today a seedling – tomorrow a flower”
Our school motto, written by one of our children and voted for by our children, encapsulates the school we are.
Every day is seen with the potential for new growth and development, and the school environment and our staff nourish and encourage this every day.
We aim to broaden the children’s outlook, experience, and personal development through a range of extra-curricular opportunities, from outdoor learning, welcoming vocational visitors, a range of clubs, our local history days, to theatre trips, whole-school art exhibitions, charity fundraisers, and debating competitions. Please look at our Personal Development Page in the Parent tab for more on this!
Through our broad curriculum, we facilitate the best academic progress through carefully sequenced lessons that build on prior learning, teaching children key skills and knowledge along the way, so that they produce high-quality, purposeful outcomes.
Our overall aim is for our children to become active contributors to the world, seeing themselves as having a significant part to play as local, national and global citizens, who make a positive difference in themselves and to others, and our 3 school values of READY – RESPECTFUL – SAFE equip our children with the necessary mind-set to achieve this.
If you are interested in seeing our school and all it has to offer, please contact the office so we can arrange a tour by our Year 6 Pupil Leadership Team.
Ms Abi Isherwood – Meare Village Primary School Headteacher

pageCache.text:

Women’s History Month
As part of March’s Women’s History month we looked at three influential and powerful queens in British history – Queen Elizabeth l, Queen Victoria and Queen Elizabeth ll. Firstly, we placed each of the queens on a time line to appreciate how long ago some of them lived. We then thought about the major changes had occurred during their reigns and how influential they were in changing things in England.We used our knowledge to design a new stamp commemorating the main changes during their reigns.

Parent Helper Team (PHT)
Parent Helper Team (PHT) is the Parent/Family association at Meare Village Primary School. It is open to all parents/carers/members of the local community and exists for the sole benefit of Meare pupils.
Fund Raising
We meet every half term in a very relaxed environment to discuss and arrange events to raise money for the children and the school. At the Christmas School Fair we raised an amazing £1,352! All the money raised goes back to the children either subsidizing activities and visits, as well as buying those items the school’s own budget can’t afford.
Can you help?
Any help, big or small is welcome. Whether you are an ideas person, a cake baker, an organizer or a shopper we will have a role for you! You don’t even have to attend meetings to be actively involved. We also welcome any ideas for fundraising events.
Easyfundraising – Did you know that whenever you buy anything online – from your weekly shop to your annual holiday – you could be raising free donations for Friends of Meare Village Primary School – Glastonbury with easyfundraising? There are over 8,000 retailers on board ready to make a donation – including eBay, Argos, John Lewis & Partners, ASOS, Booking.com and M&S – and it won’t cost you a penny extra to help us raise funds. All you need to do is:
1. Go to https://www.easyfundraising.org.uk/causes/fomearevillage/ and join for free.
2. Every time you shop online, go to easyfundraising first to find the site you want and start shopping.
3. After you’ve checked out, the retailer will make a donation to Friends of Meare Village Primary School – Glastonbury at no extra cost to you whatsoever! There are no catches or hidden charges and Friends of Meare Village Primary School – Glastonbury will be really grateful for your donations. Thank you for your support.

Seedlings
Welcome to Seedlings
Seedlings is a class of Year 1 and 2 children.
In Seedlings we know that we are only just beginning a learning journey that will last a lifetime. We aim to provide a stimulating and engaging learning environment in which the children can develop good learning habits, nourish curiosity and develop critical thinking skills. With this in mind we value questioning and discussion to support the deepening of our learning. We believe that asking questions and discussing things we encounter is invaluable to make sense of the world around us.
Seedlings also promote a culture of being openminded and value the opinions and ideas of others. We celebrate that each of us in unique and that we all have a valuable part to play in the class, school and lives of others. We respect each other and feel safe to take risks and be bold. We also value a growth mindset approach. We are not afraid to make mistakes and use them to as a valuable tool to help us persevere and develop into more resilient and reflective learners.

St Mary's Road, Meare, Glastonbury, Somerset BA6 9SP
World Book Day
The children and staff came to school dressed in their pyjamas to celebrate a love of a bedtime stories and then took part in a number of activities throughout the morning. We started with a whole school assembly where every child and adult brought along their favourite book. We talked about why we liked particular authors and spent some time with our friends sharing our books. Then, back in the classroom, we completed a number of activities such as designing our own potato book characters, making bookmarks and designing alternative front covers for our favourite books.
Most importantly we spent a lot of time just reading for the pleasure of it and sharing our enjoyment of books with each other.

Meare Village Primary School believes every child can succeed, thrive and make progress.
Every child has unique strengths and unique needs. It can be hard to know what is available and what your child is entitled to, what they need to succeed and what is typical for their age and stage of development. This area of our website provides parents and carers of children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) or parents with concerns about their child with information and advice which will signpost you to the school’s services and resources.
Getting in contact with our Special Educational Needs Coordinator
You can contact our Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENDCo) through the school office by telephoning 01458 860228, alternatively, you can use the e-mail address office@meare.school.

Emotion Coaching is an evidence-based communication strategy which helps young people to self-regulate and manage their emotions when they become stressed. Local Offer
The changes in the Children and Families Bill and the introduction of a new SEND Code of Practice, affect the way children with SEND are supported in schools. The new approach began in September 2014 and places pupils at the centre of planning. The key principles of the new legislation are:
1. Children and their families should be involved in discussions about the support they need, so they can share their knowledge and feed back to the school on the young person’s progress.2. Education, Health and Care plans (EHCPs) will replace statements of special educational needs. New assessments for additional educational needs will follow the EHCP guidelines from September 2014 (existing statements will remain in force until all children and young people have completed the transition, which will be within three years).3. School Action and School Action Plus will cease and be replaced by a single SEND support category for children who need extra specialist support. Local authorities are required to develop a ‘Local Offer’, which provides information for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) and their parents/carers in a single place, helping them to understand what services they and their families can expect from a range of local agencies.
Please click on the link below to access more information about the Local Offer.
At Meare Village Primary, teaching and learning opportunities are adapted and continually evaluated (with the support of external agencies when required) to ensure the needs of all of our learners are met. Parents should not feel unduly anxious about such additional support, as it allows learners to receive the specific help they need to make the next steps in their exciting learning journey.
If you need any further information or have any concerns, please do not hesitate to contact your child’s class teacher or the SEN team.

Anti-bullying policy
In our school, we take bullying very seriously.
We have our own code that the children know and use to show that we are all vigilant, we can all tell, and we all help to stop it.
The video below shows that our children have learned in PSHE and Anti-bullying lessons about the different types of bullying there are and the message that we should celebrate our differences!

Safeguarding
Do NOT hesitate! Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility!
To make direct contact with the Local Authority, South West Child Protection Procedures, follow the link below:Somerset Safeguarding Children Partnership (proceduresonline.com)
To email the Designated Safeguarding Lead at Meare Village Primary School: safeguarding@meare.school
Safer Recruitment Processes and Visitors to the School
The school is secure during the school day, so all visitors are asked to report to the main entrance on St Mary’s Road. Please be mindful that for everybody’s safety, identification procedures will be carried out; a copy of which are displayed in the school reception for your information.
All members of staff are vetted against national safeguarding procedures before being allowed to work in school. At least one member of every interview panel has undertaken safer recruitment training to ensure that best practices and all necessary checks are carried out.
